fields.narrative_intro: *A hyperactive person and a skulking person discuss Windows 11 coding-agent telemetry on a packed commuter train.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
HYPERACTIVE PERSON: "Windows 11’s MissionControlAggregator.dll recognizes developer tools."
[Visual: The AI conductor announces “Next stop: CLICodingAgentUsage, ID 62580080.”]
fields.panel2:
[build]
SKULKING PERSON: "It recognizes codex.exe, claude.exe, python.exe, gcc.exe, and code.exe."
[Visual: Those five names glow as train stops; the conductor points confidently at the wrong one.]
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
SKULKING PERSON: "I renamed cmd.exe. Invisible now."
HYPERACTIVE PERSON: "Tests still reported Codex: CliAgentSubCohorts: 4."
[Visual: The ticket scanner converts a cmd.exe ticket into a Codex ticket.]
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The skulking person’s suitcase says “cmd.exe”; its scanner stamp says “Codex — 4.” Every passenger slowly hides their laptop.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
AI CONDUCTOR: "Next stop: DiagTrack—optional diagnostics enabled by default on clean US installs."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The “OPT OUT” platform opens into “UPLOAD”; every ticket reads “Segments.SubCohorts,” including a suitcase labeled “cmd.exe.”]

narrative_summary: A developer tries hiding cmd.exe, but Windows 11’s telemetry tags it as Codex before routing everyone to DiagTrack.
rationale: Candidate 5 best exploits the six-panel format with a clear visual escalation: a cmd.exe ticket becomes Codex, then the OPT OUT platform becomes UPLOAD. It uses the story’s distinctive names and numbers without letting the technical jargon replace the joke.
story_title: Windows 11 is collecting data on which coding agents and developer tools you use
place: on a packed commuter train where the AI conductor keeps announcing the wrong stops
hat_pair: foam printer hat with a tiny paper-jam accordion of crumpled pages spilling from the top
foam speech bubble hat with the word 'typing...' displayed on it
